title: Bayesian Monitoring of a Diffusive Particle in One Dimension
authors: Federico Gerbino, Guido Giachetti, Pierre Le Doussal, Andrea De Luca
abstract: We study the Bayesian monitoring of a single particle diffusing along a line, while an observer tracks it continuously using noisy measurements at each spatial point. The average Shannon entropy $\overline{S(t)}$ associated with the posterior distribution of the particle's position quantifies the uncertainty that remains after conditioning on the sequence of measurements. We map the problem to the calculation of the moments of the partition functions of directed polymers in $1 + 1$ dimensions. For a constant monitoring rate, the entropy remains bounded for any finite measurement intensity and can be quantified using exact results from the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation, providing both the saturation value and the asymptotic behavior for long times. For a monitoring intensity that decreases according to a power law $\sim t^{-α}$, two distinct asymptotic regimes emerge: $\overline{S(t)} \simeq \tfrac12 \ln t$ for $α> 1/2$ and $\overline{S(t)} \simeq α\ln t$ for $0 < α< 1/2$. Both results are obtained using the replica method, which maps the problem onto an attractive Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian with a time-dependent coupling: the two regimes can be understood from a perturbative expansion around free diffusion and around the attractive Lieb-Liniger ground state, respectively. We discuss the limiting case $α= 1/2$ and compare the predictions with simulations of discrete Gaussian and log-gamma polymer models.
summary: This work analyzes how the uncertainty (measured by Shannon entropy) of a diffusing particle decreases when continuously monitored by noisy measurements. By mapping the problem to directed polymers and using the replica method, the authors derive distinct asymptotic scaling laws for the entropy based on how the monitoring strength decays over time. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding information loss in stochastic physical systems.
main_problem: The paper studies the Bayesian monitoring of a single particle diffusing in one dimension, aiming to quantify the remaining uncertainty using the average Shannon entropy.
main_result: The asymptotic scaling of the entropy depends critically on the power-law decay exponent $\alpha$ of the monitoring rate, yielding distinct logarithmic behaviors for $\alpha > 1/2$ versus $0 < \alpha < 1/2$.
method: The problem is mapped onto calculating moments of directed polymer partition functions, which is solved using the replica method and related to the attractive Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a single particle undergoing diffusion on a line, monitored by noisy local measurements. The mathematical framework involves stochastic heat equations and the replica formalism.
key_observables: Average Shannon entropy $\overline{S(t)}$, which quantifies the uncertainty remaining after measurement.
important_parameters: The monitoring rate decay exponent $\alpha$ (where $c(t) \sim t^{-\alpha}$), and the critical value $\alpha = 1/2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the continuum limit, the replica method ($n \to 1$), and approximations regarding the relative propagator evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup and plot the calculated rate of Shannon entropy versus the exponent $\alpha$, comparing different monitoring protocols.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the entropy in the diffusive monitoring problem to mapping it onto directed polymers and the Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian. It then analyzes the asymptotic behavior of the entropy in different regimes defined by the monitoring rate's decay exponent $\alpha$.
why_interesting: The connection between information theory (entropy), stochastic processes (diffusion), and advanced statistical mechanics tools (replica method, integrable Hamiltonians like LL) provides deep insights into non-equilibrium dynamics and measurement back-action.
